The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)

- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma

- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)

Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.

- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly

| 11 | `no-main-clients` | `client` | 결 | Work is proven | Show who trusted the journey | Open contact |
| 12 | `no-main-contact` | `contact` | 결 -> new 기 | Trust is established | Convert interest into a signal or brief | A new journey begins |

## Section Definitions

For section copy shape and examples, use `copy-templates.md`. For section judgment, use `review-algorithm.md`.

| Section | Must Contain | Must Not Become |
|---|---|---|
| `story` | company belief, values, convention rejected | process list, tech proof, service list |

19	```

22	
23	Ask: does this content help the user understand, trust, decide, or act?
24	
25	```text
26	Useful? -> Yes -> continue.
27	Useful? -> No -> remove it.
28	```
29	
30	Unhelpful copy often looks like:
31	
32	- clever English that adds no information
33	- a repeated claim from the previous section
34	- a phrase that cannot change user trust or understanding
35	- a large typographic block that only fills layout space
36	
37	## Section-Definition Test
38	
39	```text
40	Belongs to this section? -> Yes: refine in place.
41	Belongs to another section? -> remove here, move or save for that section.
42	Belongs nowhere? -> delete and replace with a stronger design/content role.
43	```
44	
45	Examples:
46	
47	- `story` should express company belief, values, or the convention we reject.
48	- `who` should explain the client's role and NINEONELABS role.
49	- `why` should prove capability through skills, technology, and credibility signals.
50	- `services` should name what we ship through concrete deliverables and short outcomes.
51	- If a skill list starts explaining deliverables in detail, move that detail to `services`.
52	- If a service section becomes a technology proof list, move that proof to `why`.
53	
54	## Fit Tests
55	
56	Use these only when relevant:
57	
58	- Service-fit: Does the copy match the service manifest in `services.md`?
59	- Client-fit: Does the angle match a real client situation in `client-archetypes.md`?
60	- Proof-fit: Does the claim follow `Claim -> Evidence -> Client Result` from `proof-system.md`?
61	- Positioning-fit: Does the copy explain why NINEONELABS over a plausible alternative from `positioning.md`?
62	- Process-fit: Does methodology copy match Discover · Build · Orbit in `process.md`?
63	
64	If a claim fails the relevant fit test, rewrite or remove it.
65	
66	## Context-Naturalness Test
67	
68	Ask:
69	
70	- Does the sentence follow naturally from the previous section?
71	- Does it prepare the next section?
72	- Does it steal the next section's job?
73	- Does it repeat the same rhythm or noun from nearby sections?
74	- Does it feel useful in this exact place?
75	- Does `why` still earn trust rather than list services?
76	- Does `services` still name deliverables rather than repeat proof?
77	
78	If useful but awkward, rewrite. If useful but section-wrong, move or save it.
79	
80	## Scene Comment Alignment Test
81	
82	Ask:
83	
84	- Does the section have a detailed scene comment directly above the opening `section`?
85	- Does the comment define `SCENE`, `ARC`, `PREVIOUS BEAT`, `CURRENT JOB`, `VISUAL CONTEXT`, `COPY RULE`, and `NEXT BEAT`?
86	- Does the actual copy still match the comment's `current job`?
87	- Does the actual copy prepare the `next beat` named in the comment?
88	- Do the code comment and `brand/homepage-flow.md` describe the same section role without contradiction?
89	
90	If the comment is missing or out of sync, update the comment and the copy together.
91	
92	## Adjacent-Shape Repetition Test
93	
94	Ask:
95	
96	- Do adjacent sections open with the same English rhetorical shape?
97	- Is there repeated `WE...` phrasing where a noun-led or outcome-led opening would read stronger?
98	- Does the repetition feel intentional, or merely habitual?
99	
100	If the pattern weakens rhythm, rewrite at least one adjacent heading.
101	
102	## Portfolio Proof-Grounding Test
103	
104	Ask:
105	
106	- Does the portfolio transition frame the work as launched proof rather than atmosphere?
107	- Does the body line mention real screens, shipped work, visible structure, or client-facing behavior?
108	- If a window, orbit, or launch metaphor appears, is the next line grounded in evidence?
109	
110	If the section feels scenic but not evidential, rewrite it toward proof.
111	
112	## Concept Vocabulary And Naming Test
113	
114	Ask:
115	
116	- Is every display word aligned with NINEONELABS concept vocabulary?
117	- Is the English understandable to Korean readers?
118	- Is the official name written as `NINEONELABS`?
119	- Is `nineonelabs` used only for technical context?
120	- Are mixed camel case, sentence-case, and missing-final-`B` misspellings absent?
121

123	
124	Read each line in isolation.
125	
126	- If a noun phrase is split awkwardly, rewrite.
127	- If a CTA is weakened by the break, keep it on one line.
128	- If an English function word receives weird emphasis, rewrite.
129	- If Korean subject/object/predicate balance breaks, rewrite.
130	
131	## Delete Or Redesign Decision
132	
133	```text
134	Copy removed and layout still works? -> leave markup/SCSS unchanged.
135	Copy removed and empty layout remains? -> assign a clearer content role or simplify markup/SCSS.
136	New design role needed? -> propose it before adding decorative copy.
137	```
138	
139	Design roles can be:
140	
141	- belief statement
142	- proof metric
143	- service anchor
144	- section index
145	- visual pause
146	- transition marker
147	- CTA bridge
148

```text
Belongs to another section? -> remove here, move or save for that section.
Belongs nowhere? -> delete and replace with a stronger design/content role.
```

Examples:

- `story` should express company belief, values, or the convention we reject.
- `who` should explain the client's role and NINEONELABS role.
- `why` should prove capability through skills, technology, and credibility signals.
- `services` should name what we ship through concrete deliverables and short outcomes.
- If a skill list starts explaining deliverables in detail, move that detail to `services`.
- If a service section becomes a technology proof list, move that proof to `why`.

## Fit Tests

Use these only when relevant:

- Service-fit: Does the copy match the service manifest in `services.md`?
- Client-fit: Does the angle match a real client situation in `client-archetypes.md`?
- Proof-fit: Does the claim follow `Claim -> Evidence -> Client Result` from `proof-system.md`?
- Positioning-fit: Does the copy explain why NINEONELABS over a plausible alternative from `positioning.md`?
- Process-fit: Does methodology copy match Discover · Build · Orbit in `process.md`?

If a claim fails the relevant fit test, rewrite or remove it.

## Context-Naturalness Test

Ask:

- Does the sentence follow naturally from the previous section?
- Does it prepare the next section?
- Does it steal the next section's job?
- Does it repeat the same rhythm or noun from nearby sections?
- Does it feel useful in this exact place?
- Does `why` still earn trust rather than list services?
- Does `services` still name deliverables rather than repeat proof?

If useful but awkward, rewrite. If useful but section-wrong, move or save it.

## Scene Comment Alignment Test

Ask:

- Does the section have a detailed scene comment directly above the opening `section`?
- Does the comment define `SCENE`, `ARC`, `PREVIOUS BEAT`, `CURRENT JOB`, `VISUAL CONTEXT`, `COPY RULE`, and `NEXT BEAT`?
- Does the actual copy still match the comment's `current job`?
- Does the actual copy prepare the `next beat` named in the comment?
- Do the code comment and `brand/homepage-flow.md` describe the same section role without contradiction?

If the comment is missing or out of sync, update the comment and the copy together.

## Adjacent-Shape Repetition Test

Ask:

- Do adjacent sections open with the same English rhetorical shape?
- Is there repeated `WE...` phrasing where a noun-led or outcome-led opening would read stronger?
- Does the repetition feel intentional, or merely habitual?

If the pattern weakens rhythm, rewrite at least one adjacent heading.

## Portfolio Proof-Grounding Test

Ask:

- Does the portfolio transition frame the work as launched proof rather than atmosphere?
- Does the body line mention real screens, shipped work, visible structure, or client-facing behavior?
- If a window, orbit, or launch metaphor appears, is the next line grounded in evidence?

If the section feels scenic but not evidential, rewrite it toward proof.

## Concept Vocabulary And Naming Test

Ask:

- Is every display word aligned with NINEONELABS concept vocabulary?
- Is the English understandable to Korean readers?
- Is the official name written as `NINEONELABS`?
- Is `nineonelabs` used only for technical context?
- Are mixed camel case, sentence-case, and missing-final-`B` misspellings absent?

## Line-Break Test

Read each line in isolation.

- If a noun phrase is split awkwardly, rewrite.
- If a CTA is weakened by the break, keep it on one line.
- If an English function word receives weird emphasis, rewrite.
- If Korean subject/object/predicate balance breaks, rewrite.

## Delete Or Redesign Decision

```text
Copy removed and layout still works? -> leave markup/SCSS unchanged.
Copy removed and empty layout remains? -> assign a clearer content role or simplify markup/SCSS.
New design role needed? -> propose it before adding decorative copy.
```

Design roles can be:

- belief statement
- proof metric
- service anchor
- section index
- visual pause
- transition marker
- CTA bridge

Do not preserve text just because the layout expects text.

# Voice

## Tone Principles

NINEONELABS copy should be:

- Bold: confident, not arrogant.
- Experimental: surprising only when it improves clarity.
- Precise: no filler.
- Warm at scale: collaborative without becoming casual.
- Proof-driven: grounded in shipped work, systems, or measurable outcomes.

Avoid:

- generic agency speak
- empty inspiration
- technical name-dropping without outcome
- space fantasy without service clarity
- corporate boilerplate
- overly polite sales language
- trend-chasing AI/tool language

## Korean Copy

- Use formal polite public-facing Korean.
- Keep sentences short.
- Prefer `함께`, `여정`, `브랜드`, `설계`, `경험`, `구조`, `증명`.
- Avoid `솔루션`, `최고의`, `최적의`, `고객님`.
- A Korean line break must preserve grammar and meaning when each line is read alone.

## English Copy

- Display copy may use ALL CAPS or title case depending on visual role.
- English must be understandable to Korean readers at a glance.
- Prefer short, common words over clever phrasing.
- For clear utility/proof sections, use direct nouns first: `SERVICES`, `WORKS`, `PARTNERS`, `CLIENTS`, `CONTACT`.
- Do not force journey or space metaphors into section titles when the section job is already obvious.
- Avoid repeated `WE... / WE... / WE...` headline patterns unless repetition is the concept.
- Do not stack the same English opening shape across adjacent homepage sections when a stronger noun-led or outcome-led alternative exists.
- Vary openings with nouns, objects, outcomes, or fragments: `NEW WEBSITES`, `REAL WORK`, `FROM TEST TO LAUNCH`, `DESIGNED TO PROVE`, `BUILT THROUGH FRICTION`.
- Use `NINEONELABS` for public brand display. Use `nineonelabs` only in technical/code contexts.

## Journey Language Temperature Guide

NINEONELABS의 여정/우주 언어는 제거 대상이 아니다. 섹션의 감정적 역할에 따라 온도를 조절한다.

| Temperature | Sections | Journey/Space Language | Concreteness Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Poetic (뜨거움) | `intro`, `hero`, `contact` | Full strength — the brand voice lives here | Slogan or direction-setting is enough |
| Balanced (따뜻함) | `introAction`, `story`, `who`, `partners` | Use as context, must land on a real role or result | At least one role, outcome, or action |
| Concrete (시원함) | `why`, `services`, `portfolio` | Brand tone only — lead with capability or deliverable | Specific tools, outputs, or proof required |

Rules:
- `여정` is a core brand word. Use it in Poetic sections freely. In Balanced sections, ground it with a concrete digital word (`웹`, `화면`, `구조`, `설계`).
- Removing `여정` from a Poetic section and replacing it with transactional language is always wrong.
- Contact is Poetic temperature. The CTA button label is direct (`Contact`, `Works`); the body copy stays in the brand voice.
- Maximum 4 instances of `여정` per page: 2 in Poetic sections, 2 in Balanced sections.
- The rule "every space metaphor must land on a concrete digital outcome" applies to Balanced and Concrete sections. Poetic sections may end at the metaphor when the slogan carries the meaning.

## Rhythm Rules

Do not let consecutive sections use the same copy shape.

| Scene | Copy Job | Suggested Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `intro` | invite | short English headline + 2 Korean lines |
| `introAction` | align and move | two short beats, each with a different verb |
| `hero` | land the slogan | slogan + short clarifying Korean line |
| `story` | reveal attitude | brand belief + concrete Korean proof |

| Do Not Write | Better Direction |
|---|---|
| `우리는 최고의 웹 경험을 제공합니다` | `우리가 만든 웹은 사용자가 스크롤을 멈추게 합니다` |

| `We use cutting-edge technology` | `Three.js, GSAP, and TypeScript embedded in the site you actually ship` |
| `브랜드의 가치를 높여드립니다` | `브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있을 때, 설계가 끝난 겁니다` |

## Web Agency Copy Rules

- Talk about results, not tools.
- Frame process as journey language only when it supports a concrete digital outcome.
- Every space metaphor must land on web, app, branding, UI/UX, maintenance, proof, or action.

## Skill Label Rules

- Skill labels in `why` may be short and technical, but descriptions must stay clear and outcome-aware.
- Use skill labels as proof signals, not service descriptions.
- Prefer compact pairs such as `THREE.JS / INTERACTIVE WEB`, `GSAP / MOTION & ANIMATION`, `CMS SYSTEM / CONTENT CONTROL`.

# Copy Templates

Use this file for homepage copy direction. Templates are not fixed copy; they are shape, purpose, and guardrails.

## 01. Intro

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Invite the user into the journey |
| Reader state | First visual contact |
| Message to land | This is a digital launch point |
| Shape | short English headline + 2 Korean lines |
| Avoid | abstract space fantasy |

Example:

```text
WE DESIGN YOUR JOURNEY
브랜드가 처음 세상과 만나는 순간,
웹은 가장 선명한 출발점이 됩니다.
```

## 02. introAction

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Align with the client and move toward launch |
| Reader state | Accepted the start |
| Message to land | We start beside you and turn direction into structure |
| Shape | two short beats |
| Avoid | overusing mission/signal language |

## 03. Hero

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Land the slogan |
| Reader state | Direction has become motion |
| Message to land | The journey starts on the web |
| Shape | `JOIN THE JOURNEY` + short Korean clarification |
| Avoid | remixing the slogan |

## 04. Story

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Reveal belief and rejected convention |
| Reader state | The journey has started |
| Message to land | A new brand cannot rely on default answers |
| Shape | belief headline + concrete Korean proof |
| Avoid | process lists, service lists, tech lists |

## 05. Who

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Clarify client role and NINEONELABS role |
| Reader state | Understands the philosophy |
| Message to land | The client leads; NINEONELABS builds the route and structure |
| Shape | partnership headline + role-defining Korean body |
| Avoid | making NINEONELABS the hero / stripping journey language for transactional phrases |

English headline direction: combine client-centric language with journey vocabulary.
`YOUR BRAND LEADS. WE BUILD THE ROUTE.` — `LEADS` = client is the main character, `ROUTE` = journey language + NINEONELABS role.

Example:

```text
YOUR BRAND LEADS. WE BUILD THE ROUTE.
브랜드의 방향은 클라이언트가 정합니다.
우리는 그 방향을 실제 웹 구조와 화면으로 구현합니다.
같은 여정 안에서, 함께 움직입니다.
```

## 06. Why / Skills

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Earn trust through capability and proof |
| Reader state | Knows our role |
| Message to land | We have the tools and systems to build the journey |
| Shape | compact skill labels + short proof descriptors |
| Avoid | service explanations, generic persuasion |

Example:

```text
THREE.JS / INTERACTIVE WEB
GSAP / MOTION & ANIMATION
CMS SYSTEM / CONTENT CONTROL
```

## 07. Services

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Name what we actually ship |
| Reader state | Trust is established |
| Message to land | NINEONELABS builds web, app, brand, UI/UX, and maintenance systems |
| Shape | service category + concise outcome copy |
| Avoid | raw technology list, brand philosophy |

## 08. Portfolio Intro

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Prepare evidence |
| Reader state | Understands deliverables |
| Message to land | The work became real |
| Shape | short proof-oriented transition |
| Avoid | vague gallery language |

## 09. Portfolio Detail

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Show selected work |
| Reader state | Ready for evidence |
| Message to land | This is how the system behaves in real work |
| Shape | project title + problem/result angle |
| Avoid | screenshots with no reason |

Example:

```text
FROM PLAN TO SCREEN
WORK BECOMES REAL
설계하던 구조와 경험이 이제 실제 화면과 사용 흐름으로 공개됩니다.
```

## 10. Portfolio Gallery

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Let evidence accumulate |
| Reader state | Has seen one proof point |
| Message to land | This is a repeatable standard |
| Shape | visual proof with minimal text |
| Avoid | over-explaining every item |

## 11. Clients / Partners

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Build trust |
| Reader state | Work is proven |
| Message to land | Other brands have joined the journey |
| Shape | direct title (`PARTNERS` or `CLIENTS`) + trust line + brand list |
| Avoid | inflated partnership claims, metaphor-heavy titles for simple logo lists |

## 12. Contact

| Item | Direction |
|---|---|
| Section job | Convert interest into a signal |
| Reader state | Ready to act |
| Message to land | The next journey can begin now |
| Temperature | Poetic — maintain the brand voice fully |
| Shape | Journey-persona Korean body + direct CTA button labels |
| Avoid | Stripping journey language for transactional phrases like "지금 연락하세요" |
| CTA rule | CTA button labels are direct (`Contact`, `Works`). Body copy stays in journey voice. |

The body copy must be journey-persona but include one concrete digital action or outcome.
Wrong: `새로운 여정을 위한 길은 열려 있습니다.` — passive, no action
Wrong: `새 프로젝트가 있다면, 지금 연락하세요.` — transactional, no persona
Right: Journey language + specific digital word + active verb

Example:

```text
YOUR JOURNEY STARTS HERE.

우리는 그 첫 번째 화면을 함께 설계합니다.
```
